text:
Priya (support): Hey team — urgent customer (FinSaaS) reporting p99 jump from ~800ms to ~4.2s on Dedicated during peak at 09:00 UTC. Customer says it coincided with their scheduled nightly batch. They're hitting our /v1/completions endpoint. Logs attached: `auth OK, 200`, then long wait, then `200`.
Alex (eng-sre): Noted. Do we have a timeline? Any deploys or capacity events around 08:50-09:05 UTC? @ops-bot can you dump autoscaler events for dedicated-pool-fin-prod?
ops-bot: autoscaler:deltas for dedicated-pool-fin-prod between 3123456000-3123457000:
- 08:48:12 scale request +14 -> queued
- 08:49:05 image-pull start on 3 nodes
- 08:51:30 attach success 4/14
- 08:53:00 warmup failed on 2 nodes (OOM during model init)
- 08:56:10 scaled +6 finished
Miguel (eng-runtime): OOM during model init is interesting — which model variant were they pinned to? Could be a quantization mismatch or new weights that push memory use.
Priya (support): Customer pinned to `fin-llama-7b-q4` (they confirmed). They said they did a model change to that variant yesterday but rolled back at 04:00. Not sure if anything changed on our side.
Jenna (customer-success): Customer is asking for immediate mitigation — timelines matter. They saw request latency hitting p95 and p99 for ~12 minutes (08:50-09:02). We should provide a short mitigation playbook.
Alex (eng-sre): Quick checks I'm running:
```
# check pool utilization
curl -s http://internal-api/pools/dedicated-pool-fin-prod | jq .active_shards
kubectl get pods -l pool=dedicated-fin -o wide
```
Alex (eng-sre): Findings: pool was saturated at 100% for ~3m starting 08:50, attach queue length spiked to 27, many warmups stuck because kernel image pull + model cache init overlapped with a config that sets min_pool_size=2 (too low) and concurrent_attach_limit=8.
Tom (eng-platform): We've seen this pattern: when min_pool_size is too small and image pulls are large, concurrent attach attempts thrash the provisioning queue. Suggest immediate mitigation: set a temporary outbound route to Hosted for this customer and bump min_pool_size to 6 for that pool, and increase concurrent_attach_limit to 20 to let attach ramp smoother.
Miguel (eng-runtime): Also add a throttling admission control to avoid the thundering herd: change attach_retry_backoff from 100ms -> 500ms jittered.
Priya (support): Can we do a fast action list I can give the customer? Prefer steps we can run without an infra release.
Alex (eng-sre): Fast action (no deploy):
1) Add customer-specific routing rule -> route 20% traffic to Hosted fallback for 30m. (console: Routes > Add)
2) Manually scale the dedicated pool: `poolctl scale dedicated-pool-fin-prod --min 6 --max 30`.
3) Increase attach limit: `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/provisioner CONCURRENT_ATTACH_LIMIT=20` (this picks up instantly for new attach workers).
4) Clear stuck warmup pods: `kubectl delete pod -l warmup=stuck,pool=dedicated-fin` (they'll restart and reinit)

Miguel (eng-runtime): And while we do that, enable model-fallback for the customer's route (fallback to `fin-llama-7b-q3` which uses ~30% less GPU mem) — that avoids OOMs.
Jenna (customer-success): Customer OK with Hosted fallback for 15% of traffic and a temporary min increase. Asking for RCA after.
Priya (support): Implementing steps 1-3 now. I'll update customer. @Tom can you approve the env change so I can apply? 
Tom (eng-platform): Go ahead. I'll monitor attach queue.
Alex (eng-sre): After changes: attach queue dropped to 3 within 90s, p99 back to ~880ms, p95 ~320ms. We'll keep Hosted fallback for 20% until tomorrow + run a controlled warmup sweep overnight.
Priya (support): Customer acknowledged improvement and will keep monitoring. They want a root cause and permanent mitigations.
Miguel (eng-runtime): For RCA: hypothesis chain:
- Customer pinned to a higher-memory model variant
- During their nightly batch surge, many concurrent new attaches triggered image pulls + model cache init
- min_pool_size too low -> autoscaler tried to catch up -> many concurrent attaches -> OOM on some init attempts -> retries -> attach queue thrash -> apparent p99 spike
Mitigations:
- Short-term: bump min_pool_size, increase concurrent_attach_limit, add fallback routing
- Mid-term: implement attach admission control (leaky-bucket), randomized attach backoff, prefetch kernel images and model weights for scheduled high-traffic customers
- Long-term: proactive capacity reservations for known batch windows + console option to pre-warm pinned model variants for Dedicated pools
Alex (eng-sre): I'll open a follow-up incident ticket and postmortem. Tagging as Sev-2 for now. Action owners: Alex (investigate autoscaler heuristics), Miguel (model-init memory profiling), Tom (platform knobs + console prewarm UI), Priya/Jenna (customer comms).
Priya (support): Thanks. I'll send a short customer note and link them to fallback + expected timeline for RCA. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident created #INC-2026-879 (severe: dedicated-pool saturation -> p99 spike)
